 Common Judgment

These petitions were filed by the petitioners
claiming compensation of Rs.1,00,000/ and
Rs.10,00,000/ for the injuries sustained by them in
the road traffic accident caused on 15.01.2020.
 02.

Hence these petitions were clubbed together
for the purpose of recording common evidence.

The
main petition is M.V.C.No.2425/2020 and it is clubbed
with M.V.C.No.2426/2020.
 03.

The brief facts in M.V.C.No.2425/2020 is
as under:
 It is submitted that on 15.01.2010 at about
05.30 a.m when the petitioner and Panibhushan.J
were traveling along with a goat in Auto rickshaw Cab
bearing No.AP03X8922 on Mulbagal  Punganuru
Road and when they reached near S.Ananthpura Gate,
a Goods vehicle bearing No.AP03TE2123 came in
rash and negligent manner and dashed against the
auto rickshaw cab from opposite direction.

Due to this
impact the inmates of auto rickshaw cab have
sustained grievous injuries and the auto was badly

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33708171/
2

 (Scch3) 4 MVC.No.2425/20
 c/w MVC.No.2426/20
damaged.

Immediately after the accident the petitioner
was shifted to R.L. Jalappa hospital and after first aid
he was shifted to Gaurav Orthopaedic and Surgical
hospital and admitted as inpatient.

The petitioner had
spent Rs.25,000/ towards medical expenses and
other incidental charges.

The petitioner prior to the
accident was hale and healthy and was working as
Coolie and earning Rs.750/ per day.

Due to the
accident

till today he cannot attend his work and
sustained disability and lost his earning capacity.

The
accident occurred due to the negligence of the
offending
goods vehicle driver only

. Even a criminal
case is registered against the said goods vehicle driver.

The respondent No.1 is the owner and the respondent
No.2 is the insurer of the said goods vehicle.

Hence
both respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay
the compensation to the petitioners.

Hence this
petition.

04. The brief facts in M.V.C.No.2426/2020 is
as under:

It is submitted that on 15.01.2010 at about
05.30 a.m when the petitioner and a coolie were
traveling along with a goat in Auto rickshaw cab
bearing No.AP03X8922 on Mulbagal  Punganuru
Road and when they reached near S.Ananthpura Gate,
 (Scch3) 5 MVC.No.2425/20
 c/w MVC.No.2426/20
a Goods vehicle bearing No.AP03TE2123 came in
rash and negligent manner and dashed against the
auto rickshaw cab from opposite direction.

Due to this
impact

the inmates of auto rickshaw cab have
sustained grievous injuries and the auto was badly
damaged.

Immediately after the accident the petitioner
was shifted to R.L. Jalappa hospital and after first aid
he was shifted to Gaurav Orthopaedic and Surgical
hospital and admitted as inpatient.

The petitioner had
spent Rs.1,00,000/ towards medical expenses and
other incidental charges.

Further the petitioner
required Rs.30,000/ towards future surgery.

The
petitioner prior to the accident was hale and healthy
and he was an student of 2nd year Iti electrical and
used to assist his father in agricultural operations and
was earning Rs.500/ per day.

Due to the accident till
today he cannot concentrate on his studies and cannot
attend his work and sustained disability and lost

his
earning capacity

. The accident occurred due to the
negligence of the offending goods vehicle driver only.

3

Even a criminal case is registered against the said
goods vehicle driver.

The respondent No.1 is the owner
and the respondent No.2 is the insurer of the said
goods vehicle.

Hence both respondents are jointly and
 (Scch3) 6 MVC.No.2425/20
 c/w MVC.No.2426/20
severally liable to pay the compensation to the
petitioners.
Hence this petition.

05. After service of notice, the respondent No.1
had not appeared before this court on the date fixed
for his appearance and hence he was placed absent
through out the proceedings of both the petitions.

However the respondent No.2 have appeared through
their counsel and filed written statement in both
petitions.

06. The averments of the written statement of
the respondent No.2 in both petitions are as under :
 This respondent has not issued package policy in
favour of the respondent No.1.

Hence no question of
indemnifying the respondent No.1 arise.

The
respondent No.1 has to prove that the said policy was
in force at the time of accident.

That the offending
goods vehicle was not involved in the accident.

The
respondent No.1 has not intimated about the accident.

The accident took place due to the negligence of auto
driver.

Hence the petition is bad for nonjoinder of
necessary parties.

The offending goods vehicle driver
was not holding valid driving licence on the date of
accident.

It is denied that due to the accident the
petitioners have sustained disability and lost income
as stated in the petitions. This respondent has denied
 (Scch3) 7 MVC.No.2425/20
 c/w MVC.No.2426/20
the manner of accident, injuries and income as stated
by the petitioners.

These petitions were filed in
collusion with police and respondent No.1 in order to
make unlawful gain.

The claim of the petitioners are
excessive and prays to dismiss all petitions with costs.

07. In order to prove the case, the petitioners in
both petitions and the Doctor were examined
themselves as Pw.1 to 3 and got marked 22
documents as per Ex.P.1 to 22 and closed their side.

08. By way of rebuttal, the respondent No.2
submits no oral evidence.

However the copy of policy
was marked as Ex.R.1 with consent.

09. Heard both sides in both petitions.
 10.

Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the
following issues have been framed: 
 Issues In M.V.C.No.2425/2020

 has sustained simple injuries in the accident
 occurred on 15.01.2020 at about 05.30 a.m,
 on Punganuru  Mulbagal Road, near
 S.Ananthapura Gate, Mulbagal Taluk, Kolar,
 due to rash and negligent act of the driving of
 goods tempo bearing reg. No.AP03TE2123
 by its driver as alleged in the petition ?

(Scch3) 8 MVC.No.2425/20

 compensation?

Issues In M.V.C.No.2426/2020
 01.

Whether the petitioner proves that he
 has sustained grievous injuries in the accident
 occurred on 15.01.2020 at about 05.30 a.m,
 on Punganuru  Mulbagal Road, near
 S.Ananthapura Gate, Mulbagal Taluk, Kolar,
 due to rash and negligent act of the driving of
 goods tempo bearing reg. No.AP03TE2123
 by its driver as alleged in the petition ?
 02.

Whether the petitioner is entitled for
 compensation?

If so, to what amount & from
 whom?
 03.
What order or award?

11. My findings on the aforesaid issues are as
under:
 Issues In M.V.C.No.2425/2020
 Issue No.1 : In affirmative
 Issue No.2 : In partly affirmative
 Issue No.3 :

c/w MVC.No.2426/20
 Issues In M.V.C.No.2426/2020

Issue No.1 : In affirmative
 Issue No.2 : In partly affirmative

 Issue No.3 : As per final order
 for the following:

Reasons
 12. Issue No.1 in M.V.C.No.2425/2020 and
issue No.1 in M.V.C.No.2426/2020:

These issues
will be taken at one stretch for my consideration as
they are inter related with each other and common in
order to avoid repetition of facts.

It is the grievance of the petitioners that they
have sustained grievous injuries due to the rash and
negligent driving of goods vehicle driver bearing No.
Ap03Te2123.

Due to the accident they have
sustained disability and lost income.

The same was
opposed by the respondent No.2 and contended that
the accident did not took place due to the negligence of
offending goods vehicle driver and it is due to the
negligence of auto driver.

The insured vehicle is falsely
implicated in this case in order to claim compensation.

Hence they are not liable to pay the compensation to
the petitioners.

(Scch3) 10 MVC.No.2425/20
 c/w MVC.No.2426/20
 13. To prove this, the petitioner of
M.V.C.No.2425/20 was got examined himself as Pw.1
by reiterating all the averments of the petition in his
affidavit.

The Pw.1 in his cross examination has
admitted that "That on the date of accident I was
proceeding towards sandy.

Along with me one pani,
auto driver, Gangadhar and two goats were present in
the auto.

There is 30-40 kms distance in between my
village and said sandy.

I cannot say the speed limit of
the auto in which I was proceeding.

It is true that as I
was seated back side of auto, I do not know how the
auto was moving.

It is true that I cannot say at what
speed limit the opposite vehicle was coming.

It is true
that even now I am doing coolie work with some
difficulty.

It is true that I took treatment as inpatient
for one day as it was too expensive".

Apart from this
the Pw.1 had denied other suggestion of the
respondent No.2 counsel.

14. Further another injured and the claimant in
M.V.C.No.2426/2020 was got examined himself as
Pw.2 by reiterating all the averments of the petition in
his affidavit.

In his cross examination he has admitted
that " It is true that I am an student.

We were three
persons including the driver in the auto.

It is true that
as I was seated at backside I cannot say which vehicle
 (Scch3) 11 MVC.No.2425/20
 c/w MVC.No.2426/20
In: Sri.S.Muniswamy vs In: 01. Sri.Mohammed Badrulla Khan on 16 February, 2023

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33708171/
6

was coming from our opposite direction.

That I got
discontinue of my studies due to accident.

It is true
that I have no difficulty to read and write, but I have
difficulty to lift any object".

Apart from this the Pw.2
had denied all suggestion of the respondent No.2
counsel.

15. The Pw.1 and 2 in support of their case got
marked entire police documents at Ex.P.1 to 5, 13 and
19.

So on perusal of these documents, it is clear that
the concerned I.O after investigation has filed
chargesheet against the offending goods vehicle driver
for the alleged offences punishable U/Sec 279, 337,
338 and 429 of Ipc stating that the petitioners have
sustained injuries and the goat died due to rash and
negligent driving of offending goods vehicle driver only.

16. It is true that eventhough the respondent
No.2 contended that the accident does not took place
due to their insured goods vehicle driver, but to prove
this they have not adduced any supportive oral and
documentary evidence.

Even the mahazar and Imv
report got marked supports the version of the
petitioners

. So on perusal of all police records
accompanied with the oral evidence of the Pw.1 and 2
and in absence of rebuttal evidence by the respondent
No.2 in this regard, it is true that the petitioners have
 (Scch3) 12 MVC.No.2425/20
 c/w MVC.No.2426/20
proved that the offending goods vehicle was involved in
this accident and its driver due to his negligent driving
had caused the accident which leads to injuries to
them.

17. Therefore with the available oral and
documentary evidence, it is true that the petitioners
have proved that they have sustained injuries due to
the rash and negligent driving of the offending goods
vehicle driver.

Hence I answered the issue No.1 in
M.V.C.No.2425/2020 in affirmative and issue No.1
in M.V.C.No.2426/2020 in affirmative.
 18. Issue No.2 in M.V.C.No.2425/2020 and
issue No.2 in M.V.C.No.2426/2020: These issues will
be taken at one stretch for my consideration as they
are inter related with each other and common in order
to avoid repetition of facts.

19. Further the petitioner in
M.V.C.No.2425/2020 has stated that due to the
accident he is not able to do work as earlier and
sustained disability.

In this regard he had not got
examined any witnesses or not produced any
documents to show his disability.

Even the Pw.1 has

Sri. Mohammed Badrulla Khan
on 16 February, 2023

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33708171/
7

not produced any documents to show his income or
loss of income.

Even there are no documents to believe
that the petitioner has sustained disability and not
 (Scch3) 13 MVC.No.2425/20
 c/w MVC.No.2426/20
able to work as earlier.

Even there are no documents
to show that the petitioner has required future
treatment.

Hence this petitioner is not entitled for any
amount under the head of loss of future income and
future medical expenses.

20 . Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for the
compensation under the following heads:
 a).

Pain and sufferings during treatment
period: The petitioner has stated that he was
admitted in hospital as inpatient.

But in this regard he
had not produced any documents.

Hence under these
circumstances considering the injuries sustained by
the petitioner, I just feel it proper to award
Rs.20,000/ under this head as the petitioner might
have spent amount when he took treatment either as
inpatient or outpatient.
 b).

Towards medical expenses: This petitioner
has got marked medical bills, prescriptions, Ct scan
report, ultrasound report and outpatient record as per
Ex.P.6 to 10.

The respondent No.2 have not objected
for these documents.

Hence the petitioner is entitled
for Rs.6,365/ under this head.

c). Loss of income during laid up period:-
Admittedly the Pw.1 as per available records could not
 (Scch3) 14 MVC.No.2425/20
 c/w MVC.No.2426/20
do any work for about 15 days after the accident.
Hence, he is entitled for Rs.7,000/ under this head.

d). Loss of amenities and nutrition food:-
The Pw.1 had not produced any documents to show
that he had incurred amount towards amenities and
nutritious food.

But looking into the period of
treatment and the nature of injuries, I just feel it
proper to award a sum of Rs.10,000/ under this
head.

e). Towards attendent charges and
conveyance: The Pw.1 has not produced any
discharge summary to show that he took treatment
either as inpatient.

But he had produced only
outpatient record.

Hence under these circumstances I
just feel it proper to award a sum of Rs.2,000/
towards taking treatment as outpatient under this
head.

21 . Therefore, the petitioner in M.V.C.
In: Sri.S.Muniswamy vs In: 01. Sri.Mohammed Badrulla Khan on 16 February, 2023
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33708171/
8

No.2425/2020 is entitled for total compensation of
Rs.45,365/ (Forty five thousand three hundred
and sixty five only ).
 22.

Further the petitioner in
M.V.C.No.2426/2020 has stated that due to the
accident he is not able to do work as earlier and also
discontinued his studies and sustained disability.

In
 (Scch3) 15 MVC.No.2425/20
 c/w MVC.No.2426/20
this regard PW.2/petitioner has got examined the
Orthopedic Surgeon/Senior Consultant as Pw.3 who
had stated that petitioner had undergone open
reduction and internal fixation with plate and screws
done to left tibia. Radiological examination revealed
fracture shaft of middle one third of right humerus
shows union with implants in situ.

23. The Pw.3 had assessed physical disability at
36.41% and 12.13% to whole body.

The Pw.3 has got
marked outpatient record, mobility component and
Xray as per Ex.P.20 to 22.
 24.

The Pw.3 in his cross examination has
admitted that "It is true that the fractures are united.

It is true that the petitioner can do normal work with
some difficulty.

It is true that as the petitioner is aged
about 20 years fractures will be united soon.

The
implants are in situ.

It is true that the implants can be
removed at Government hospital at free of cost".
 25.

Hence, from the evidence of Pw.3 and from
Ex.P.20 to 22, the petitioner has sustained disability
due to the accident, but not as stated by the Pw.3.

Hence under these circumstances, I just feel it proper
to consider 10% disability for the petitioner.

26 . Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for the
compensation under the following heads:
 (Scch3) 16 MVC.No.2425/20
 c/w MVC.No.2426/20
 a).
Loss of future income:

The Pw.2 has stated
that he was assisting his father in agriculutral
operation and earning Rs.500/ per day and also
studying Iti.

In this regard he had not produced any
documents to show that his father had any
agricultural land or he was studying and discontinued
his studies.

Hence, in the absence of such documents,
I just feel it proper to consider the notional income.

As
on the date of accident the notional income can be
fixed at Rs.14,500/.

The Pw.2 had stated that he was
aged about 20 years at the time of accident.

In this
regard the Pw.2 has got marked his aadhar card as
per Ex.P.17
which reveals
that the Pw.2 was born

In: Sri.S.Muniswamy vs In: 01. Sri.Mohammed Badrulla Khan on 16 February, 2023
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33708171/
9

19.09.2001.

Hence as per Ex.P.17 it is just and proper
to consider the age of the petitioner as 19 years at the
time of accident.

Thereby proper multiplier comes to
"18".

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for loss of
future income as Rs.14,500 x 12 x 18 x 10/100 =
Rs.3,13,200/ under this head.

b). Pain and sufferings during treatment
period: The petitioner has stated that he was
admitted in hospital as inpatient.

In this regard he had
got marked the Discharge summary as per Ex.P.14
which shows that the petitioner was admitted as
inpatient from 15.01.2020 to 18.01.2020.

Hence under
 (Scch3) 17 MVC.No.2425/20
 c/w MVC.No.2426/20
these circumstances, I just feel it proper to award
Rs.25,000/ under this head.

c). Towards medical expenses: The petitioner
has got marked entire medical bills and prescriptions
as per Ex.P.15 and 16 which amounts to Rs.70,247/.

There is no serious dispute with regard to other
medical bills produced and marked by the petitioner.

Hence the petitioner is entitled for Rs.70,247/ under
this head.
d). Loss of income during laid up period:-

Admittedly the Pw.2 as per available records could not
do any work for about 1 month after the accident.
Hence, he is entitled for Rs.14,500/ under this head.
e). Loss of amenities and nutrition food:-

The Pw.2 had not produced any documents to show
that he had incurred amount towards amenities and
nutritious food.

But looking into the period of
treatment and the nature of injuries, I just feel it
proper to award a sum of Rs.10,000/ under this
head.

f). Towards attendent charges and
conveyance:

The Pw.2 was admitted as inpatient for
nearly 03 days.

In these days the petitioner has to look
after by some body.

Hence under these circumstances
 (Scch3) 18 MVC.No.2425/20
 c/w MVC.No.2426/20
I just feel it proper to award a sum of Rs.3,000/
under this head.
g). Towards future medical expenses:

The
Pw.3 has stated that the Pw.2 required future surgery
for implant removal from right humerus.

Hence under
these circumstances I just feel it proper to award a
sum of Rs.15,000/ under this head.

27. Therefore, the petitioner in M.V.C.
No.2426/2020 is entitled for total compensation of

Indian

Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33708171/
10

Rs.4,50,947/ (Four lakhs fifty thousand nine
hundred and forty seven only).
28. Regarding liability : The respondent No.2

eventhough denied issuance of the policy in the name
of the respondent No.1 in their written statement but
they have got marked the copy of policy with consent
as per Ex.R.1.

So on perusal of Ex.R.1 the said policy
was in force at the time of accident.

It is true that the
petitioners have proved that the accident occurred due
to the rash and negligent driving of the offending goods
vehicle driver.

The said offending goods vehicle was
owned by the respondent No.1 and insured with
respondent No.2

. Hence both respondents are jointly
and severally liable to pay compensation to the
petitioners.

Hence I answered the issue No.2 in
M.V.C.No.2425/2020 in partly affirmative and
 (Scch3) 19 MVC.No.2425/20
 c/w MVC.No.2426/20
issue No.2 in M.V.C.No.2426/2020 in partly
affirmative.
 29. Issue No.3 in M.V.C.No.2425/20 and
issue No.3 in M.V.C.No.2426/20: These issues will
be taken at one stretch for my consideration

as they
are inter related with each other and common in order
to avoid repetition of facts.

Further as per my above findings on above and
with regard to awarding the interest is concerned, the
petitioners in both cases are entitled for simple interest
at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition
till deposit.

As such I proceed to pass the following :
 Order
The claim petition filed by the petitioner in M.V.C.No.2425/2020 U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act is partly
allowed with costs.
The petitioner in M.V.C.No.2425/2020 is entitled for Rs.45,365/ (Forty five tho
usand three hundred and sixty five only)
as compensation with interest at 6% p.a from the date of petition till the date of deposit

. 
The respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

However, in view of valid insurance policy, (SCCH3) 20 MVC.No.2425/20 c/w MVC.No.2426/20 respondent No.2  Insurance Company is directed to pay the total awarded amount and shall deposit the same within time stipulated under section 168(3) of M.V. Act.

On deposit of the compensation amount together with interest accrued, the Office is directed to release the entire amount in the name of petitioner through Epayment on proper identification In: Sri.S.Muniswamy vs In: 01. sentences.text: The claim petition filed by the petitioner in M.V.C.No.2426/2020 U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner in M.V.C.No.2426/2020 is entitled for Rs.4,50,947/ (Four lakhs fifty thousand nine hundred and forty seven only) as compensation with interest at 6% p.a (the interest awarded is not applicable to future medical expenses of Rs.15,000/) from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

However, in view of valid insurance policy, respondent No.2  Insurance Company is directed to pay the total awarded amount and shall deposit the (SCCH3) 21 MVC.No.2425/20 c/w MVC.No.2426/20 same within time stipulated under section 168(3) of M.V. Act.
On deposit of the compensation amount together with interest office to release entire amount to the petitioner through Epayment on proper identification without any further proceedings.
The original Judgment shall be kept in M.V.C.No.2425/2020 and copy of the same shall be kept in M.V.C.No.2426/2020.
The advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/ each.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated directly to the Stenographer on computer, got typed by him, corrected and then pronounced by me in open court, on this the 16th day of February 2023).
(SHILPA.K.S) VII Addl. Judge and ACMM, Bengaluru.

 Order
